questions.def: Gerunds (verb+ing) can act as nouns, the subject of a sentence.
questions.question: ___ is important for good health.

questions.def: Gerund phrases can function as the subject of a sentence.
questions.question: ___ early is a good habit.

questions.def: "Going to bed early" is the noun phrase required.
questions.question: Go to bed early helps you feel better.

questions.def: A gerund (walking) acts as a noun – the subject.
questions.question: ___ is good exercise.

questions.def: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (verb+ing).
questions.question: I enjoy ___ books in my free time.

questions.def: After 'at', use the gerund (verb+ing) form.
questions.question: He is good at ___ languages.

questions.def: Use the noun form: swimming.
questions.question: The swim in the ocean was refreshing.

questions.def: The gerund 'writing' functions as the subject.
questions.question: ___ is my favourite hobby.

questions.def: A gerund is needed as the subject of this sentence.
questions.question: ___ is not always easy.

questions.def: Spent time + gerund (verb+ing).
questions.question: She spent hours ___ the piano.

questions.def: 'Driving' is a gerund acting as a noun (subject).
questions.question: ___ is a useful skill.

questions.def: After "about", use the gerund (verb+ing).
questions.question: He is thinking about ___ a new car.

questions.def: A gerund (swimming) acts as a noun (subject).
questions.question: ___ is a popular sport.

questions.def: A gerund (speaking) acts as a noun (subject).
questions.question: ___ English is useful.

questions.def: Gerund used as a noun subject.
questions.question: ___ less sugar is good for you.

questions.def: After the preposition 'in', use the gerund.
questions.question: I am interested in ___ new things.

questions.def: After 'enjoys', use the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: She enjoys ___ novels.

questions.def: Use 'Traveling' as a gerund acting as a noun.
questions.question: ___ can be fun.

questions.def: After 'of', use the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: He is tired of ___.

questions.def: A gerund 'playing' is needed as the subject.
questions.question: ___ video games is his hobby.

questions.def: Gerund as subject: Learning is good.
questions.question: ___ is good for your mind.

questions.def: After 'of', use the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: She is afraid of ___ alone.

questions.def: The gerund 'sleeping' functions as the subject.
questions.question: ___ is important for health.

questions.def: Gerund: Listening helps me.
questions.question: ___ helps me relax.

questions.def: 'Stopped' is often followed by a gerund.
questions.question: He stopped ___.

questions.def: Using a gerund (exercising) makes the verb act as a noun.
questions.question: ___ is important for everyone's health.

questions.def: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (reading), which acts as a noun.
questions.question: I enjoy ___ books in my free time.

questions.def: Using 'walking' as a gerund makes it the subject of the sentence.
questions.question: ___ is a good way to get around.

questions.def: The gerund 'talking' functions as the subject in this sentence.
questions.question: ___ is not allowed in the library.

questions.def: 'Waking up' (gerund phrase) acts as a noun, the subject.
questions.question: ___ early is a good habit to have.
